summary: IDS s154_double is degraded: 10.4% oversize frames (>1518B, up to 8058B) dropped by 1Gbps IDS NIC and 10.1% TCP packets show missing data due to broker slicing. Both cause silent detection gaps for payload-based signatures.

findings.root_cause: 227 of 2185 frames (10.4%) exceed the IDS port MTU of 1518 bytes (largest 8058 bytes). Likely jumbo frames or encapsulated traffic forwarded without MTU conditioning; the IDS NIC drops oversize frames before inspection.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS silently loses ~10% of frames. Any attack or C2 in large/jumbogram frames is invisible, creating systematic detection blind spot.

recommended_fix.why: IDS needs full payload but cannot receive frames >1518B. Enable jumbo-frame support (MTU 9000) on IDS NIC and packet-broker egress, or configure broker to handle MTU conditioning without slicing, so large frames are delivered intact instead of being dropped.

findings.root_cause: 212 of 2101 TCP packets (10.1%) show sequence gaps by IP-length analysis and the feed is sliced. Broker payload slicing/truncation is cutting packets short, breaking TCP reassembly.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires full payload for stream reassembly and signature matching. Sliced packets cause missing data, failed reassembly, missed exploits and increased false negatives/evasion risk.

recommended_fix.why: Disable snaplen/slicing on the packet broker for this IDS feed to deliver full packets. Combine with jumbo-MTU fix above so full-size frames are not dropped after disabling slicing.
